title: Adaptive Security Intake & SLA Negotiation Playbook for High-Risk Enterprise Requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise sales and account teams routinely surface high-effort security and compliance asks (SOC2 evidence, custom DPAs, HIPAA scoping, ISO questionnaires and bespoke vendor security questionnaires). Current intake is ad-hoc: requests land in email/Slack, are forwarded to security, then manually prioritized — leading to long SLAs, inconsistent negotiation outcomes, and missed upsell/trial conversion windows.

Goal: Design a repeatable, adaptive intake and prioritization playbook that: 1) automatically classifies incoming security/compliance asks by regulatory domain and risk profile; 2) assigns an SLA and negotiation template based on impact and contract stage; 3) provides prescriptive escalation paths and negotiation guidance for account teams; and 4) integrates with existing ticketing and the Console so customers get predictable commitments.

Scope: This ticket covers product management work to define the playbook and the intake routing rules, the SLA table (commitments and response templates), negotiation fallback options (e.g., canned DPA clauses, scoping checklist), and a pilot plan with two strategic customers. Engineering and Design tickets will be created for implementation (automation rules, Console UI changes, notification templates).

Out of scope: Full implementation of automation rules across all channels (will be phased), new legal language drafting (Legal will own DPA text), and wholesale changes to pricing or contract terms.

Proposed solution:
- Create a classification matrix that maps ask types (SOC2 evidence request, ISO questionnaire, HIPAA scoping, GDPR/DPA negotiation, third-party security questionnaire) to a risk tier (Low/Medium/High) based on data sensitivity, contract stage, and customer size.
- Define SLA bands and recommended negotiation templates per tier: e.g., High-risk (P0) -> 5 business days initial response + assigned security lead; Medium-risk (P1) -> 10 business days + templated answers; Low-risk (P2/P3) -> 20 business days + self-serve guidance and docs.
- Build an intake form + triage rules in the internal ticketing flow to capture required metadata (customer, product surface, data processed, contract stage, requested artifacts, deadline).
- Produce a playbook for AE/AM/CS to follow during negotiations: escalation steps, fallback model variants for private deployments, recommended timeline for Dedicated/Private customers, and when to involve Legal/Security/Engineering.
- Create a small pilot with two enterprise customers to validate SLAs, measure time-to-resolution, and capture friction points.

Success metrics:
- Median time-to-first-response for high-risk asks reduced from current baseline to <= 5 business days.
- Pilot NPS from account teams >= 80 for clarity of next steps.
- 75% of incoming questionnaires correctly auto-classified by rules in pilot period.
acceptance_criteria: Classification matrix defined and approved by Security and Sales
SLA table with response templates and assigned owners published
Intake form prototype created and linked to ticketing workflow
Negotiation playbook drafted and reviewed by Legal and Security
Pilot plan (2 customers) with measurement plan and success metrics
Roadmap items created for Engineering and Design work to implement automation
